sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: International Time-Definite Small Parcel Courier Operations

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code lineage with autonomous hybrid commercial legislation)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) — ensures extended territorial application of BITs entered into by Belgium (e.g., BLEU–China BIT signed 2005, in force 2009; BLEU–India BIT signed 1997, in force 2000)
Luxembourg–United States Double Tax Convention (signed 3 Apr 1996, as amended by Protocol of 20 May 2009, in force 30 Nov 2011)
Luxembourg–China DTA (signed 23 Mar 1994, amended by Protocol of 11 Nov 2014, in force 13 Nov 2015)
Luxembourg–United Kingdom DTA (effective 1 Jan 2025 under BEPS MLI multi-lateral instrument framework)
EU Pillar II Directive (2022/2523) global minimum 15% top-up tax implemented via Law of 20 Dec 2023

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE, Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs); Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (LML/FTR, as consolidated by Laws of 17 July 2008 and 12 May 2022); CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 of 14 December 2012; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 18 June 2020 on RBE filings; EU Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD5); CJEU judgment of 22 November 2022 (C-37/20, C-601/20) restricting public RBE access; Luxembourg Law of 5 December 2023 re-implementing proportionate legitimate-interest access.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (post-CJEU: RBE registers are confidential to the public; access granted solely to FIU Luxembourg (Cellule de Renseignement Financier), CSSF, tax authorities, notaries, and bailiffs; any person/firm proving a legitimate interest may apply for restricted disclosure before the competent court)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Owner Declaration and Ultimate Beneficial Ownership Identity Statement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate registry or national civil registry of each 25%+ shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the origin state (2025: all G7 states are Hague parties); non-Hague states require full Consular Legalization chain via Luxembourg Embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Excerpt of commercial register for any corporate UBO (piercing intermediary entities)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of Commerce / Companies House of the intermediary jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (with certified translation into French/German/English required if not in French)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified True Copy and Apostille of Passport/National ID of each ultimate natural-person UBO and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or consular officer in country of nationality/residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; note: Luxembourg notaries (notaire) performing the incorporation deed are statutorily required to verify UBO identity under RBE Law Art. 6

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter / Confirmation of Source of Funds (for each UBO funding share capital; €12,000 minimum SARL capital)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A credit institution licensed in EU/EEA or a bank rating >= A- in the country of formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Standard banking letterhead is accepted; apostilization is required only if a foreign notary-certified signature is relied upon

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Summary of the Notarial Deed on Incorporation (existing name search report to RCS and Chamber of Notaries database)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary (notaire) worstelling via LBR API portal
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial signature, no apostille required (internal public document under Article 15 of the Notarial Law of 9 August 1998)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Registered Office (domiciliation) Agreement from an approved société de domiciliation or leased office contract
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified legal services provider or independent lessor registered with RCS
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille not required if EU counterparty; for non-EU lessor, apostille + French translation required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory real-time multi-list screening of each UBO, director, manager and POA holder against: (i) EU consolidated financial sanctions list (CFSP), including Council Regulation (EU) 833/2014 and implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/4; (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) A simple, written recommendation to use OFAC SDN-list as a red-flag only and of Luxembourg Grand-Ducal Regulation dated 24 December 2024 to freeze all Russian/U-asset exposure; (iv) CSSF AML/CFT circular CSSF 18/704 (updates 2024) and FATF High-Risk List screening of the country of registered office (Luxembourg: no additional AML measures vis-à-vis its own jurisdiction); (v) financial penalty of up to EUR 5,000,000 for organisation v. AML breaches (LML Art. 8-1), therefore the notary and the RBE administrator must obtain signed PEP self-declaration by each UBO.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — https://www.lbr.lu — operational platform of the RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) and the «Electronic platform of the Ministry of Justice» for name availability checks and incorporation filings.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A SARL name must be submitted in Latin script exactly as transliterated on the natural-person identity documents. If the chosen name is Franco-Germanic or Latin-script, no translation is required. If the applicant uses Cyrillic/Arabic/Chinese characters, the RCS accepts a phonetic or semantic transliteration into French or German accompanied by a certified translation. All statutory references to the corporate name in the articles of association must be identical to the registered version. The name must not be contrary to Luxembourg public policy or misleading as to the corporate activity (e.g., a courier company cannot include 'bank' or 'insurance').
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Luxembourg — requires prior ministerial authorization from the Ministry of Economy under RCS practice (Art. 1 para. 4 of Law of 19 Dec 2002)
Bank, Banque, Crédit, Épargne, Caisse — requires CSSF (Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier) prior authorization (Law of 5 Apr 1993 on the financial sector)
Assurance, Insurance, Réassurance — requires Commissariat aux Assurances (CAA) authorization (Law of 7 Dec 2015)
État, State, State of Luxembourg — prohibited without special ministerial dispensation
Fond d'investissement, SICAV, FCP, Fund — requires CSSF authorization under Law of 17 Dec 2010 on undertakings for collective investment
Société, SARL, Holding, Anonyme — cannot be used if the actual corporate form does not match or if the company is not yet incorporated
Loi, Réglementation, Justice, Tribunal, Police — suggested as irreconcilable with public order

Express Couriers, Customs Brokering, Tax Agency — cannot imply regulated activity unless appropriate license held (ISIC 5320 requires an EU/EЭС operating authorization for courier services under Regulation (EU) 2018/644, so the RCS will reject name tokens suggesting a postal universal service license is held when only a parcel courier license is obtained)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS/name clearance rejects a proposed corporate name, the applicant (or notary acting on behalf) must: (1) receive a written refusal notice from RCS naming the conflicting prior registration; (2) request a formal written reason from the Registrar via LBR portal within 8 business days; (3) file an administrative appeal (recours) with the District Court of Luxembourg (Tribunal d'arrondissement) sitting in commercial matters within 2 months of notification of refusal, pursuant to Article 21 of the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies; (4) alternatively, apply for an extension of the 30-day reservation by refilling the same name application after expiration, which is customarily granted if no third party has claimed the name in the interim.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible. Luxembourg fully accepts registered-office agreements with licensed sociétés de domiciliation (commercial domiciliation service providers governed by Article 1-1 of the Law of 19 December 2002 and monitored by the Ministry of Justice) for the registered address. However the Courier Express business (ISIC 5320) requires the possession of an actual operational base in Luxembourg (staffed loading/sorting facility or contractual access to a warehouse of a licensed EU authorized courier), which the virtual office cannot replace; otherwise the RCS considers the company to be a 'letterbox' entity and may apply commercial-substance solvency tests under Article 710-3 of the Law of 10 August 1915.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium risk — approximately 15-25% annual probability of unannounced RCS or Customs/AVL physical inspection in Luxembourg for cross-border courier registrations; the presence of a Licensed Postal Operator (LPO) declaration and harmonized hold-and-verify records of EU CJR (Customs Judicial Register) raises inspection likelihood to 30% in the initial operating year.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration Fee for Notarial Deed of Incorporation (SARL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary (notaire) — fees set by Grand-Ducal Regulation of 12 May 1993 (statutory tariff on subscribed capital; EUR 1,200-1,600 prevailing benchmark)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff plus liability review

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS Entry Fee (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Ministry of Justice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Grand-Ducal Regulation tariff — EUR 69 standard RCS registration for SARL

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the Incorporation Extract in the Electronic Companies and Associations Bulletin (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Justice / RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO RBE Register Filing — declaration of beneficial owners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) on behalf of Finance Ministry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutorily free of charge in 2025 for initial submission; annual consistency filing also free

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial Certified Copy of Passports/ID and Document Authentication (apostille chain for foreign UBOs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary + Ministry of Foreign Affairs (apostille service) in UBO country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Foreign Ministry statutory rate of origin state (range USD 8-50 per apostille; broker fee EUR 60-120 per doc)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Translation into French/German of Foreign Corporate Documents (Certificate of Incumbency, POA, Bank Reference)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Court-certified translation provider (traducteur assermenté) registered with Luxembourg district court
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark EUR 30-60 per 250-word page, minimum 3 pages; Lux Court tariff all-in standard

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Domiciliation Services — Registered Office Agreement (Year-1 Fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Société de domiciliation licensed under Art. 1-1 of Law of 19 Dec 2002
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark EUR 2,200-2,800 per annum for fully serviced address with mail forwarding and compliance annex

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation Legal Counsel Fee — UBO Piercing, AML KYC, Name Clearance, and Notarial Drafting
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg avocat (Barreau de Luxembourg) with corporate/AML practice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hourly rate benchmark EUR 350-450; fixed fee customary for standard SARL incorporation at EUR 4,500-6,000 including name clearance and notary coordination

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Anti-Money-Laundering Software Screening Fee (PEP/OFAC/Sanctions — per UBO)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Integrated check is executed by the law firm/ notary — no external registrar fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Covered within legal counsel fee; a standalone World-Check renewal would be EUR 1,200/yr — here deemed internal

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Difference for SARL Minimum Capital Lock-up — EUR 12,000 (non-budget operational)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg bank account / RCL notary escrow for capital deposited before incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Not a cost — capital reserve; 25% must be paid up before notarial deed (€3,100 minimum)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Professional Contribution to the Ordered Professional Institution (Bar contribution for incorporation deed)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed tariff EUR 100-150 per notarial file covering chamber stamps and judicial verification

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Arts. 710-1 to 710-24 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée); Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies and accounting (Loi du 19 décembre 2002 concernant le registre de commerce et des sociétés et la comptabilité).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS), administered by the Luxembourg Business Registers and the Ministry of Justice; filing is performed through the eJustice.lu central electronic portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) setting out the articles of association (statuts), filed with the RCS and published in the Electronic Collection of Companies and Associations (Recueil électronique des sociétés, RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital EUR 12,000 for a SARL, fully subscribed and paid up at incorporation; cash contributions must be deposited in a special blocked escrow account held by the Luxembourg notary (compte bloqué) and released only upon issuance of the RCS registration certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers hereby form a Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL) under the laws of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and irrevocably subscribe to and take up all shares in the founding capital of EUR 12,000, which has been fully paid into escrow. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is established at [address], Luxembourg, and the directors are authorized to execute the lease and notify the RCS. RESOLVED, that [Name A] is appointed as sole manager (gérant) and [Name B] as authorized signatory, each with powers to act within the legal limits, and that the managers are directed to apply for all required courier-operating licenses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and notarization of the articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public in Luxembourg, Chamber of Notaries (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Luxembourg notary to prepare the French-language statuts, verify the legality of the corporate object, and execute the deed before the notary. Submit the proposed name, registered office, share capital, and manager identity to the notary prior to execution.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association including company name, registered office, corporate object, capital, and share classes
Valid passports or national identity cards of all subscribers and the proposed manager
Bank confirmation of the escrow deposit for the cash contribution
Name reservation certificate from the RCS, if obtained
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS rejects the proposed name, the notary amends the statuts and re-executes the deed. If the capital evidence is incomplete, execution is postponed until the bank block attestation is provided.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution or the notary's blocked escrow account (compte bloqué)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transfer the full EUR 12,000 cash subscription to a special blocked account opened in the name of the SARL in formation. Obtain an attestation from the bank confirming that the funds are irrevocably blocked until the RCS registration certificate is issued. If contributions are made in kind, obtain the statutory auditor's valuation report.
required_dossiers: Payment order to the notary's escrow account
Bank attestation of capital blocking and non-repayment (attestation de blocage)
Statutory auditor's valuation report for contributions in kind, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to issue the block attestation, open an escrow account at another Luxembourg credit institution. If the in-kind valuation is queried, an independent expert valuer must be appointed and a revised report filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register and RESA publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through the eJustice.lu online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarial deed and the electronic RCS registration form through the eJustice.lu platform. Pay the applicable registration fee. After approval, the RCS assigns the registration number, and the extract is published in the RESA within the statutory timeline.
required_dossiers: Original or certified copy of the notarial deed of incorporation
RCS electronic registration form
Bank block attestation confirming the paid-up share capital
Identity documents of the manager(s)
Power of attorney if filing is made by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises a query, the notary submits an explanatory addendum or corrective document within three working days. If the application is rejected, the full dossier may be resubmitted; the initial registration priority is lost unless the defect is cured before the statutory deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social security registration with the CCSS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) - Luxembourg Joint Social Security Center
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company and its managers and employees electronically through the guichet.lu portal or by filing the CCSS employer registration form. Obtain the employer registration number and declare employees before any work commences.
required_dossiers: RCS extract (extrait du registre) showing the company registration number
Identity cards and Luxembourg national identification numbers of managers
Employee registration declarations
Bank details in Luxembourg for social security contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CCSS delays registration, supply the RCS certificate and legal form details; any late-registration penalty may be waived on presentation of proof of the actual activation date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the VAT registration form (Formulaire 1) to the AED within fifteen days of incorporation if the courier activity will be subject to Luxembourg VAT. Obtain the Luxembourg VAT number, open an eFiling account, and activate the electronic tax mailbox. Set up the accounting system consistent with the Luxembourg chart of accounts.
required_dossiers: RCS extract confirming the corporate name and registered office
Luxembourg IBAN bank account details
Detailed description of the principal activity (ISIC 5320 express courier)
Identification of any approved VAT representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AED requests further documentation, supply the corporate object, pro-forma invoices, and estimated turnover schedule. If the VAT number is not required due to exemption thresholds, obtain an official written exemption confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy - Business Establishment Licensing Department (Direction générale des classes moyennes) via guichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the autorisation d'établissement under the Law of 2 September 2011 on the exercise of commercial activities. Demonstrate managerial integrity, professional competency, and availability of suitable premises. The permit must be obtained before the actual commencement of express courier operations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of no criminal record (casier judiciaire) for each manager
Proof of professional competence or relevant experience in express courier or logistics
Lease agreement for registered office and sorting depot
Site plan and floor layout for the depot
Identity documents and professional references
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is refused, an administrative appeal may be lodged with the Minister of Economy within forty days. If the refusal is based on insufficient professional competence, the applicant may cure the deficiency by submitting accredited training certificates or documented prior experience.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) for the commercial establishment permit; Ministry of Mobility and Public Works (Ministère de la Mobilité et des Travaux publics) for road transport licensing of commercial vehicles used in the courier operation.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) under the Luxembourg Law of 2 September 2011; supplementary national road-freight operating license under Regulation (EC) No 1071/2009 if vehicles exceed 3.5 tonnes.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Administration)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration/declaration-tier only if the sorting depot or warehouse floor area exceeds 500 m² or if operations fall within Annex V EIA thresholds; a full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is not required for standard express courier depots except where hazardous waste storage, major combustion installations, or habitat damage is involved; otherwise exempt from EIA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges into municipal sewage must comply with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 22 December 1994 on urban wastewater limit values; petroleum storage must use double-walled tanks with leak detection; vehicles must meet applicable EU emission standards, generally Euro 6d-TEMP for light freight; packaging waste take-back and recovery obligations apply under the Law of 21 March 2017 and related waste-management regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance from the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Service (Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours, CGDIS) or municipal fire inspector for the office and sorting depot; structural load certificate from a certified engineering office validating floor capacity for shelving and parcel handling; workplace safety and health clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) under the Luxembourg Labour Code, including evacuation plans and occupational risk assessment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) — Direction de la TVA (VAT), and Administration des douanes et accises (customs/exports); direct taxes: Administration des contributions directes (ACD). Official portals: MyGuichet.lu, guichet.lu, impotsdirects.public.lu, and Luxembourg Business Registers (lbr.lu) for RCS filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Luxembourg SARL: (1) notarized incorporation deed filed with the RCS via MyGuichet.lu/LBR, automatically generating the 13-digit national matricule (RNPPM) used as the ACD corporate TIN; (2) file the AEDT 'Demande d'immatriculation à la TVA' application through MyGuichet.lu indicting the intended start date, ISIC 5320 activity, estimated turnover and place of effective management; the AEDT issues the LU-prefixed 8-digit VAT number normally within 10 business days; (3) non-EU-established entities must appoint a jointly and severally liable Luxembourg VAT representative unless an EU mutual assistance convention applies; (4) registration is mandatory from the first taxable supply for non-established operators and express transport businesses — no de minimis threshold applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope: resident SARL taxed on worldwide profits at a combined standard rate of 24.94% in Luxembourg City (IRC 17% + solidarity surcharge 7% + municipal business tax 6.75%); SARL has no pass-through eligibility; participation-exemption regime under Article 166 LIR excludes qualifying dividend and capital-gain income at entity level; net wealth tax applies only where balance sheet total exceeds EUR 350,000; loss carryforward of 17 years with annual offset cap (EUR 1m plus 75% of the exceeding income).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Group fiscal unity election under Article 164bis LIR (95% capital link, Luxembourg and EEA resident subsidiaries may join and fully offset profits/losses); participation-exemption election at 10% shareholding or EUR 1.2m acquisition cost with 12-month holding condition; hybrid mismatch disallowances under ATAD (Luxembourg law of 21 December 2018) with limited elective structuring options; VAT grouping election ('assujetti unique') under Article 60(1) of the VAT law for financially integrated Luxembourg entities; MOSS/IOSS registration options for digital and distance services; no separate check-the-box classification exists for SARL.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration threshold for non-established suppliers or for cross-border express courier services; taxable persons must register from the first euro of Luxembourg taxable supplies. Domestic micro-undertakings may claim the Article 57 small-enterprise exemption as long as annual turnover remains below the statutory threshold (EUR 30,000–35,000 band as indexed by AEDT guidance), but the exemption is excluded for export, intra-Community and transport services and for all ISIC 5320 operations. The intra-EU distance-sales threshold of EUR 35,000 applies to foreign e-commerce traders shipping low-value parcels to Luxembourg consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg has no real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping system: the AEDT relies on periodic VAT returns (eTVA/eCDF) and European Sales Lists (recapitulative statements) filed electronically. Mandatory structured e-invoicing (EN 16931, UBL/CII) for domestic B2B invoices enters into force on 1 January 2026 under the law of 15 December 2023, transmitted via a registered PEPPOL access point; in the interim, PDF/paper invoices remain valid, and any e-invoice must stay machine-readable. Courier consignments require no transaction-level clearance, but each invoice must bear the issuer's LU VAT number and, for intra-EU dispatches, the customer's VAT ID; continuous transaction controls are planned only under the EU ViDA framework (not yet in force).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (exemption with deduction) applies to: (i) goods exported to a non-EU destination under Article 42 of the VAT law, proven by physical departure from the EU within the statutory period; (ii) intra-EU B2B dispatches to a customer holding a valid EU VAT ID verified in VIES; and (iii) international transport of goods carried partly or wholly outside the EU, plus freight-forwarding services directly linked to export, import or intra-Community transit under Article 43 of the VAT law. For ISIC 5320 express parcel operations, the operator must maintain route-level scan events and transport evidence (AWB/B/L/CMR) demonstrating each parcel's international character; administrative goods shipped under ICC rules qualify only with an export declaration. The reduced (8%) and intermediate (16%) Luxembourg VAT rates do not apply to transport; domestic courier legs are standard-rated at 18% unless the supply qualifies as ancillary to an export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Validated customs export declaration (SAD/EX, electronic AES record) for non-EU shipments
Transport documents matching the shipment route: master/route air waybill, bill of lading, CMR, or equivalent scan-event transit log of the express courier network
Commercial invoice and packing list with Incoterms, parcel value, and HS classification codes
Intra-EU dispatch: customer VAT ID validated in VIES, invoice kept in the seller's records, and matching EC Sales List line
Proof of payment and, for Chinese parent groups, the SAFE outward-collection record/inward remittance certificate evidencing repatriation within the 180-day window
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEDT may reassess zero-rated exports for up to 5 years (10 years in fraud cases); failure to produce the complete documentation bundle within the audit deadline reclassifies the supply as taxable at the standard rate, triggering repayment of deducted input VAT, late-payment interest at 0.6% per month, and administrative penalties under Article 61 of the VAT law (up to 10% for negligence and up to 100% of the evaded tax for intentional concealment, plus criminal exposure). Customs post-clearance recovery (AFA) may be raised by the Administration des douanes et accises within 3 years of the export declaration. Repeated irregularities block the exporter's VAT refund account and may lead to revocation of the zero-rating authorization and compulsory periodic audits of the courier's IT systems.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting in conjunction with the European Central Bank (ECB) within the Eurosystem; the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) supervises credit institutions and fintech/licensed entities for prudential and AML matters.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full, unrestricted convertibility of the euro for both current-account and capital-account transactions. Luxembourg applies Article 63 TFEU and Council Directive 88/361/EEC guaranteeing free movement of capital; no exchange-control approvals, no surrender obligations, and no differentiated treatment of resident versus non-resident foreign-currency accounts apply. Profit remittances are freely executable provided the company maintains a proper corporate authorization (shareholder/board resolution), filed annual accounts, and satisfies statutory withholding mechanics (15% dividend withholding tax, potentially reduced under an applicable double taxation treaty); no prior CSSF or BCL consent is required for such remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation exists in Luxembourg. There is no mandatory conversion ratio or statutory timeline for repatriation of export receipts; the entity may freely hold, convert, or deploy foreign currency. However, residents sending or receiving cross-border payments equal to or exceeding EUR 12,500 per transaction must enable their bank to submit Balance-of-Payments (BoP) statistical declarations to the BCL under the BCL external-statistics framework and CSSF Circular 13-01 and related reporting rules; the underlying economic purpose code must classify transport/courier service fees (EU BoP classification for transport services).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Epargne de l'Etat, Luxembourg (Spuerkeess / BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte de blocage) and Operational Current Account in EUR and USD
Operational Account with integrated corporate e-banking API for courier collections; Capital Escrow Account available
Operational Account and multi-currency current accounts with dedicated trade-finance desk
Operational Account with SWIFT corporate e-banking and global payment rails
Operational Account (preferred for corporate groups with Southern European counterparties)
Operational Account; more suited to advisory and private-banking treasury services than high-volume settlement

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with strict legal constraints. Luxembourg-registered E-Money Institutions (EMIs) licensed by the CSSF under the Payment Services Law of 2009 (implementing Directive 2009/110/EC and PSD2) may operate multi-currency business accounts, issue payment cards, route SEPA and SWIFT payments, and passport across the EEA. However, EMIs cannot grant credit, cannot issue or confirm documentary Letters of Credit, and must ring-fence client funds in safeguarding accounts. They are therefore highly viable for high-volume parcel-payment collection and payout disbursement rails (card settlement and SEPA direct debit) but not for primary capital-escrow, borrowing, or documentary-credit treasury functions. The recommended pattern is a hybrid architecture: EMI-controlled collection and disbursement rails swept daily into a Tier-1 Luxembourg commercial bank for liquidity concentration and capital operations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg law (AML Law of 12 November 2004 as amended; CSSF Regulation 12-02; CSSF Circular 22/849) requires reliable verification of every director, authorized signatory, and beneficial owner. In practice, Tier-1 banks require at least one physical appearance of the ultimate beneficial owner and the managing director(s), or an in-person verification performed by a Luxembourg notary or by an embassy/consulate for non-resident principals; purely remote opening remains within the bank's discretion and is rarely granted for SARL accounts lacking an existing group relationship. For the SARL incorporation capital, the notary's blocked-account attestation (attestation de blocage) is mandatory before registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCSL).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border express courier profile flagged for transit-trade money laundering risk (cash-equivalent logistics flows across multiple jurisdictions)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transport service contracts with airlines and postal operators; detailed commercial invoices; customs declarations (CN22/CN23 or electronic equivalent) per shipment lane; proof-of-delivery (POD) logs; client KYC files for all corporate shippers; reconciliations between the sales ledger, collection reports, and bank statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity of the Luxembourg SARL (risk that UBOs are offshore or layered)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RBE (Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs) registration certificate; up-to-date shareholders register and notarized corporate documentation; UBO identity documents and power-of-attorney chains; organizational chart clearly linking the entity to ultimate individuals; tax-residency certificates of each UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and export-control exposure due to global shipment destinations (EU consolidated sanctions list, OFAC, UN embargoes)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions-screening policy and historical denied-party screening logs; restricted-commodity classification (dual-use and export-control license assessment); destination-jurisdiction risk matrix; annual AML/CTF officer attestations; contractual exclusion clauses with specific air waybill embargo lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume payout and receipt asymmetries to third-country carriers (red flag for invoice manipulation and value transfer)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Inter-company settlement agreements with open-book terms; counterparty corporate KYC including audited financials of carriers; per-country invoice aging schedules; evidence of commercial substance; explanation memos for currency mismatches; board-approved transfer-pricing file per OECD Chapter V.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash and card collections concentration from small merchants (unexpected high-frequency card-not-present transactions)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant underwriting files; merchant due-diligence and chargeback histories; terminal and acquiring settlement reports; sub-merchant monitoring framework; withdrawal-frequency thresholds; daily reconciliation to the courier delivery manifest system.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocol for a capital injection into the Luxembourg SARL: (1) instruct the parent or shareholder to originate an SWIFT MT103 from the remitting bank to the Luxembourg bank (IBAN LU... and BIC of the Luxembourg credit institution); (2) the instruction must state the reason for payment as 'equity contribution / souscription au capital de la SARL'; (3) the receiving bank will require the notarial deed of incorporation or a capital-increase notarial deed, the blocked-funds attestation (attestation de blocage) for the SARL minimum capital (EUR 12,000 for a standard SARL, or EUR 30,000 for a SARL-S meeting the simplified regime conditions), and evidence of the source of funds; (4) for statistical reporting, the receiving bank records the economic purpose under the EU BoP classification 'Direct investment - Equity capital' and submits the return to the BCL if the credit equals or exceeds EUR 12,500; (5) after RCSL registration, the blocked funds are released into a fully operational account, and the company files financial statements reflecting share capital and any share premium.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The express-courier treasury uses a tiered clearing architecture: (a) intra-EEA euro disbursements to partner consolidators and last-mile carriers execute via SEPA Credit Transfer (SEPA CT) with reference codes aligned to the clearance ledger; (b) cross-border non-euro settlements (airline lift fees, outbound gateway handling, and US/UK/Asia partner fees) execute via SWIFT MT103 with the proper BoP purpose codes such as 'transport services - courier fees' or 'business services'; (c) for large-value imports of specialized logistics equipment or consignment-goods flows, a Commercial Letter of Credit (sight or deferred) and documentary collections are used, with the Luxembourg Tier-1 bank as issuing bank and the advising bank in the supplier jurisdiction; (d) settlement reconciliation is anchored to the delivery-management system's POD records, with cut-off liquidity ratios maintained per clearing lane; and (e) FX concentration accounts with an in-bank notional pooling overlay provide real-time visibility into the currency grid.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX Forwards (deliverable between EUR and USD, GBP, CHF, JPY, and other convertible currencies) permitted without BCL authorization, subject to the bank's ISDA/CSA credit documentation and CSSF EMIR reporting thresholds

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on restricted currencies (notably CNY, INR, NGN, and certain emerging-market currencies required by courier destination lanes) permitted on an outright basis for hedging future invoicing exposure; OTC contracts require EMIR trade reporting, margining where applicable, and a board-approved hedging policy

Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) for matching longer-duration receivable and liability structures when the SARL capitalizes logistics assets or when intra-group funding is denominated in a non-euro currency; permitted for hedging under EU EMIR and PRIIPs frameworks, requiring confirmation templates and collateral arrangements

European-style FX Options (calls and puts) available through Tier-1 banks and licensed FX desks for asymmetric hedging of volatile emerging-market collection currencies, subject to quarterly stress testing and board risk limits
Platform auto-conversion sweeps used solely for settlement-fee minimization on e-commerce payment gateways (not speculative), reconciling daily against ACH and card settlement curves

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (Comptes Annuels) filing and publication
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) / Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year-end (e.g., 31 July for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers an RCS formal reminder and a criminal misdemeanour; fines range from €500 to €10,000; repeated default may lead to judicial strike-off (radiation) of the SARL.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (RBE annual declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) administered by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month following the anniversary of the RBE initial registration; also required within 1 month of any change to beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or inaccurate confirmation is an AML compliance violation; administrative fines up to €25,000; wilful false declarations may attract imprisonment of 6 days to 5 years and/or fines up to €1,250,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual approval of statutory accounts by shareholders’ general meeting (corporate secretarial act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the SARL (minutes filed in the company’s statutory archives; no fee)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after financial year-end (prior to the RCS filing deadline)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the general meeting can invalidate the annual accounts approval process; directors may face civil liability and tax administration penalties for untimely filing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit by an independent réviseur d'entreprises agréé if, for two consecutive financial years, the SARL exceeds at least two of three thresholds: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average headcount of 50.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002, implementing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS-EU allowed optionally for standalone annual accounts; consolidated accounts of public-interest entities must comply with IFRS-EU.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For a SARL, share transfers must be notarized and recorded in the RBS registry of shares; the RBE must be updated within one month of the transfer. Annually, regardless of any change, the SARL must file an explicit confirmation that the RBE data remains accurate, no later than one month after the anniversary of the initial RBE registration. The RBE only discloses UBO ownership percentage bands, not exact percentages.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City combined rate: 17% corporate income tax + 7% state solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box regime: 80% exemption of qualifying net IP income producing an effective rate of approximately 4.99%; 15% tax credit for digitalisation investments; 20% tax credit for environmental transition investments; statutory investment tax credit on eligible tangible/intangible assets; partial relief for certain qualifying finance income; SME-friendly accelerated depreciation offsets.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 600C (Corporate Income Tax Return) and combined filing for municipal business tax and net wealth tax; submitted electronically via the Luxembourg direct tax administration e-filing portal (MyGuichet.lu / e-CDF).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (single fiscal-year return; no quarterly income tax returns required for ordinary commercial SARLs).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 March of the year following the calendar year-end; for a fiscal year not aligned with the calendar year, the deadline is the last day of the third month after fiscal year-end; administrative extensions to 30 June are commonly granted upon timely request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gross worldwide commercial revenue unless a permanent establishment allocation applies. For an express courier company include parcel delivery fees, cross-border transport charges, tracking and logistics surcharges, and fuel surcharges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities carrying on business through a Luxembourg permanent establishment enter only the Luxembourg-attributable turnover under the relevant DTA Article 7 business-profits allocation; attach a PE statement and transfer-pricing schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim deductible expenditure directly connected with taxable income: driver/employee wages, VAT-exclusive fuel and tolls, aircraft/vehicle lease rentals, subcontractor courier costs, customs brokerage fees, insurance premiums, depreciation, and arm's-length intercompany back-office charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents deduct only expenses economically connected with Luxembourg PE income; intercompany service and logistics charges must be supported by contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation and invoices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 — Taxable Result after IP Box and Loss Offset
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate net commercial result after commercial depreciation, shutdown of loss-making routes, IP box relief on qualifying routing software or courier-process patents, and unused losses. Luxembourg does not allow carryback; losses offset current-year profit in the applicable order.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident PE must apply the same deduction ordering and substantiate that the IP box benefit arises from Luxembourg taxable activity, not from a shell arrangement designed merely to access the 80% IP exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 — Foreign Tax Credits and Withholding Tax Reconciliations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resident companies report inbound foreign-source courier revenue and claim credit or exemption for foreign withholding taxes under an applicable DTA; detail underlying taxes on dividends, interest, and royalties from subsidiary or branch operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents with only a Luxembourg PE generally do not receive foreign tax credit in Luxembourg for foreign taxes borne on PE profits unless a DTA requires restriction; all DTA-creditable amounts require completed Form 770 and foreign TRC evidence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an administrative surcharge of up to 10% of the assessed tax (minimum EUR 250, maximum EUR 10,000 per return), plus late-payment interest of 0.6% per month from the initial statutory due date. Failure to file after formal notice can escalate to fines up to EUR 250,000 and, in cases of fraudulent non-declaration, imprisonment of up to five years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic Luxembourg dividend withholding tax, reduced to 0% under qualifying EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive conditions or under income tax treaties providing full relief; 5% or 10% treaty rates may apply for portfolio investors depending on the relevant DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced or zero treaty rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the competent foreign tax authority, complete the Luxembourg withholding-tax exemption or refund form (Form 270/270a or the applicable EDPF electronic refund request), identify the relevant DTA article, demonstrate actual entitlement to the income and beneficial ownership, and provide signed declarations on the absence of abusive conduit arrangements. The Luxembourg payer may apply the reduced rate at source after the tax administration validates the request; otherwise, the excess is recovered through a formal refund procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law imposes no withholding tax on outbound interest or royalty payments to non-resident corporate recipients: interest 0%, IP royalties 0%. Treaty rates are consequently not triggered at source, but European Union Interest and Royalties Directive relief remains relevant for EU-resident associated entities; all payments should nevertheless be documented with beneficial-ownership certificates because anti-abuse rules may reclassify equity-like loans or excessive royalties as constructive dividends exposed to the 15% dividend WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Luxembourg Local File preparation applies when the Luxembourg taxpayer engages in related-party transactions exceeding EUR 1,000,000 annually; a Master File is required when the multinational group maintains consolidated revenue of at least EUR 50,000,000; Country-by-Country Report thresholds follow the OECD BEPS standard at consolidated group revenue of EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but enforces an economic-substance doctrine through statutory general anti-abuse rules (GAAR), ATAD measures, administrative circulars, and case law. Cross-border express courier holding or financing entities must demonstrate real personnel, business premises, decision-making independence, and actual operational activity; a shell SARL lacking substance will be denied treaty benefits, EU directives, and Luxembourg tax rulings, and may trigger immediate reassessment and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Corporate Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting cross-border courier revenues, submitting forged or inflated fuel/leasing invoices, recording fictitious subcontractor payments, concealing Luxembourg-source income in foreign accounts, or signing a knowingly false Formulaire 600C declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of all under-declared taxes and 0.6% monthly late-payment interest; criminal fine under Article 426 of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law of up to EUR 250,000; imprisonment up to five years; seizure or disqualification from courier operating licences; public disclosure of conviction in aggravated cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who signs or causes a false return is jointly and severally liable for the full tax deficiency; piercing the corporate veil permits civil restitution from personal assets; criminal courts may impose travel bans, confiscation orders, director disqualification, and imprisonment of up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing cross-border intra-group courier services at non-arm's-length rates, failing to prepare Local/Master Files, executing round-trip service invoices, maintaining thin capital structures, or claiming management fees from tax-haven entities without operational substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary transfer-pricing adjustment to Luxembourg taxable profit; penalty surcharge of 20% of the upward adjustment; late-payment interest of 0.6% per month; administrative fines up to EUR 250,000; cancellation or retroactive revocation of advance pricing agreements or tax rulings when facts are misstated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally exposed where they engineered tainted intercompany pricing or directed creation of shell counterparties; courts may pierce the veil to recover unpaid corporate tax and interest from personal assets; criminal liability for fraudulent accounting documentation can lead to travel bans, disqualification, asset freezes, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Dividend Withholding Tax / Profit Repatriation Avoidance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Making distributions to shareholders without complying with the 15% Luxembourg withholding tax, disguising dividends as interest or royalties, using circular loans to strip profits without substance, or claiming treaty relief without valid beneficial-ownership evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of uncompensated dividend withholding tax plus 0.6% monthly interest; administrative fine up to EUR 10,000; criminal prosecution for fraudulent withholding-tax evasion with fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to five years; denial of all treaty and EU directive relief for abusive schemes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for unpaid withholding tax if they knowingly structured the distribution or if the company is a mere facade; piercing the corporate veil yields direct civil restitution from directors' personal assets; travel bans, extradition proceedings, and imprisonment are available where concealment through foreign bank accounts is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Beneficial Ownership / Shell Company Substance Breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing false ultimate beneficial owner declarations in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Interests, failing to identify the true owner of the SARL, using courier invoicing to launder third-party funds, retaining nominee directors without decision-making authority, or failing to maintain genuine business substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004 as amended: fines up to EUR 1,250,000 and imprisonment up to five years; mandatory deregistration from the Luxembourg trade register; freezing of funds and confiscation of proceeds; revocation of the courier operating licence and denial of VAT registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate veil is pierced: directors are civilly liable for restitution of laundered amounts, personally fined and disqualified; courts may issue travel bans, order extradition, freeze personal and corporate assets, and impose imprisonment; each director can be held criminally responsible if they knew or recklessly ignored the unlawful provenance of funds.
